Why Digital Skills are Vital for Ghanaian Youth

The Digi-Health Impact Project combined digital skills training and SRHR education, reaching 720 beneficiaries in Ketu South District with support from KGL Foundation.

Connecting digital skills and health education

The Digi-Health Impact Project (DHIP), supported by KGL Foundation, brought digital skills training and sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) education to high school students in Ketu South District. The project reached 720 beneficiaries.

Practical tools for the future of work

Training covered Microsoft Office Suite, graphics design, and cybersecurity. These skills supported young people’s digital literacy and employability, helping them prepare for the modern workplace.

Information for informed decisions

Alongside digital training, an SRHR education campaign equipped participants with reproductive health knowledge. The project connected preparation for work with the information young people need to make informed decisions about their health.
